title: Finding 3 is only partly fixed: the shot clock still counts after the move while the move waits to commit, and then it jumps back up
scenario: Phone at 390x844 on a slow CPU (the 10x phone from finding 5; at 4x the window is shorter). A model is thinking and the ring shows 31 (30.6 s left). The viewer's first touch starts the stats' transition render (StatsScreens.tsx:76; on a desktop it starts as soon as the stats chunk loads). 0.1 s later the llm_action arrives with 30.5 s left, so the hold is 31. Its setTables call (useGameState.ts:51) is a DefaultLane update. getNextLanes keeps the transition in progress ahead of it, so the move waits until the stats commit: about 0.5 s at 4x, over 1 s at 10x. The draw timer runs between the render's 5 ms slices. It reads the clock from the last commit, which is still running (useSecondsDraw.ts:23, called from Player.tsx:96 and ReasoningPanel.tsx:47). At the 30 s edge it draws 30, and on a 10x phone also 29. The engine has neither value: its clock stopped at 30.5 s. When the move commits, the layout effect draws the hold, 31. The desktop text reads 31, 30, 31, and the ring sweeps back up. The old flushSync committed the move at the edge. Now nothing does. 'Next hand in Ns' has the same defect when an outage game_state replaces dealAt: it counts 3, 2 against the old deal, then shows 177s. clock-stops-at-move cannot see this. It ignores every value within 550 ms of the move, and it tests 'back up' only on the next turn.
fix: Make the draw read the latest state that arrived, not the last commit. In useGameState, keep a ref that the stream handler updates on arrival (latest.current = applyMessage(latest.current, m, at); setTables(latest.current)). Expose getters for its clock and dealAt. Each step of useSecondsDraw calls the getter, and it stops rescheduling once that clock has stopped. The hold then starts when the move arrives, whatever React is rendering.
verifier: Confirmed from the code. useGameState.ts:51 calls setTables inside the EventSource 'message' event. The bundled react-dom gives that update DefaultLane: resolveUpdatePriority calls getEventPriority('message'), which returns 32. The stats mount is startTransition(() => setOn(true)) (StatsScreens.tsx:76). It runs at once on a desktop and on the first gesture on a phone. The bundled getNextLanes keeps a work-in-progress transition ahead of a DefaultLane update: `32 === nextLane && 0 !== (wip & 4194048)` returns wipLanes. So the llm_action waits until the stats render and commit end. The render yields every 5 ms, so useSecondsDraw's timer runs between slices. Its ms closure (Player.tsx:96, ReasoningPanel.tsx:47) holds the last committed clock, which still has running set to true. The second edge therefore draws one second below the hold. When the move commits, the no-deps layout effect redraws from stoppedAt, which is the move's arrival time (`at`). That value is one second higher, so the text reads 31, 30, 31 and the ring sweeps back up. Before the range, the edge's flushSync committed the waiting DefaultLane update (getHighestPriorityLanes takes lanes & 42), so nothing counted on a stale clock. The window is real at 4x. The later replay-fixes trace puts StatsSections' render at 150-200 ms, CumulativeChart at about 240 ms, and the one commit near 1 s. clock-stops-at-move ignores every value within 550 ms of the move and tests 'back up' only on the next turn, so it passes. The countdown half is weaker, because all table state waits the same way. But the shot clock shows a value the engine never held and then goes back up.
verifierFix: In useGameState, apply each message to a ref when it arrives (latest.current = applyMessage(latest.current, m, at); setTables(latest.current)) and expose a getter for its clock and dealAt. In useSecondsDraw's step, read that getter's clock when it belongs to the same turn as the committed one (same `received`), and stop rescheduling once it has stopped. A move that has arrived then holds at once, whatever React is rendering. Optionally, make clock-stops-at-move also fail on any value below the hold after the move.

title: Left open: on a slow CPU, the shot clock and the countdown stay on screen up to about 1 s past their second while the stats load (clock-after-load is red)
scenario: 1440x900 on a 4x CPU, page loaded mid-turn. About 3.5 to 4.5 s after the load, the stats chunk's evaluation and mount run as main-thread tasks of 0.8 to 1.1 s (FIX-REVIEW4.md, long-task trace from DEBUG_CLOCK=1). The draw is a main-thread setTimeout, so the step for the second edge cannot run during those tasks. The panel keeps showing 36s with 35 s left, and the felt keeps showing 'Next hand in 4s' with 3 s left, for up to about 1 s. That breaks 'never a second more than the engine's'. The run's own clock-after-load fails on this branch with exactly these values. The run left it open and did not loosen the check.
fix: While a clock or a countdown runs, keep every main-thread task below the check's 300 ms slack on a 4x CPU. Split the stats chunk and its mount (StatsScreens.tsx:76) into smaller pieces and commits. Or move the digits off the main thread, for example a strip of digits moved by a compositor transform. Do not loosen clock-after-load.
verifier: Confirmed at 9e41df2, and still partly open at the branch head. useSecondsDraw's step is a main-thread setTimeout (line 25). The whole wide stats mount in one transition (StatsScreens.tsx:76), and its commit ran as one task of 0.8 to 1.7 s on a 4x CPU. FIX-REVIEW4.md measured this, and the later replay-fixes trace names the causes: the one-commit mount, CumulativeChart rebuilding 19 lines, and motion's layout measurement. No draw can run during that task. So the stricter clock-after-load fails on this branch ('clock 36s still shown with 35s left; countdown 4s still shown with 3s left'). That breaks the hook's own rule that it 'never shows a second the engine no longer has'. The defect is older than the range (the base build fails too), but the run reported it open and did not loosen the check, so the range left it. Line 25 is where the defect shows. The cause is the stats' long tasks. After the range, 11771f4 (the five-part mount) and 16ada94 (memoised lines) cut the longest task to about 0.46 s. But clock-after-load still failed 2 of 3 runs alone (replay-fixes/REPLAY-FIXES.md), so it is not fixed at the head either.
verifierFix: Keep the five-part mount and the memoised lines. Then split the work that is left, mainly motion's layout measurement of the Profiles and Matchups `layout` figures at each part's commit, across more tasks. Stop when no task after the load is longer than about 250 ms at 4x and clock-after-load passes 3 of 3 runs alone. Another option is to draw the digits off the main thread. Do not loosen clock-after-load.

title: A zoom now trims 5% of its points off each end and draws them flat along the plot's edge, so the line disagrees with the readout and the zoomed stretch is clipped again (review 3 #9)
scenario: Setup: 1440x900, the opened Trends card at rest, Chips metric, nine seated lines. Chips has no fitAt, so before 10e130d nothing in a chips zoom was ever held at the edge. The viewer pinches into hands 300–700. In that stretch the leader X climbs from +3,000 to +8,000 chips by hand 480, then falls back to +4,500 by hand 650. The other eight stay within ±2,000. Line 594 pools about 1,440 samples (9 lines × 160), and line 599 trims them 5–95%. q1 is the 73rd-highest sample, which is X's own value of about +5,870. The right quarter's must tops out near +5,530, so Y1 is about +6,500 after the 8% air. path() (line 637) now clamps every point of a zoom. X's hands from about 425 to 555, a third of the window, are drawn as a flat 2px line along the top edge, above the top gridline. There is no arrow, because only tips get one. When the viewer hovers hand 480, the readout says 'X +8,000 chips', but X's dot and line sit at about +6,500. The same thing happens to a line shown on its own (the others switched off in the legend): its top and bottom 5% of samples in the left three quarters are flattened. A bb/100 leader's peak in the middle of the window is flattened the same way. Before this range, every fitted point of a zoom was in robustRange's must, so the zoomed stretch was drawn whole. That was the review 3 #9 fix ('the stretch zoomed into is not clipped at the plot's edges'). Owner rule: a figure on screen that disagrees with the engine's numbers is mission-critical.
fix: Do not trim the stretch the viewer zoomed into. In a zoom, put the window's points from cut = lerp(X0, X1, 0.75 × zoomWidth / fullWidth) into must, untrimmed. At full width that is the rest fit's right quarter, and a narrow zoom fits its whole stretch. Remove the `zoom ||` clamp from path(), so a point outside that range is clipped as it is at rest. Keep holding only the points before fitAt. Never trim the chips metric.
verifier: Confirmed at 9e41df2. CumulativeChart.tsx:594 passes every in-view point as robustRange's vs, so it is trimmed to the 5th-95th percentile. Line 599's must holds only the right quarter, the tips and ahead, and ahead is empty at rest. Line 637's `zoom ||` clamps every zoomed point to [Y0, Y1]. At e0806b1 a zoom put every fitted point in must, and chips (fitAt empty) were never clamped. So this is a real regression of the review 3 #9 fix. I re-ran the scenario's numbers. trace gives about 160 samples a line, so 9 lines give 1,440. q(0.95) = s[1367], the 73rd-highest sample, about +5,870. The right quarter tops out at about +5,530, and Y1 comes to about +6,500 after air. X is above that from about hand 426 to 553, so a third of the leader's stretch is drawn flat on the top edge. No marker shows it, because only tips get the off-axis arrow. Nothing else widens the fit at rest: the later `far` logic needs perS > 0, which means a replay is playing. One part is overstated. A line shown alone loses only samples beyond q +/- 8% air, not its whole top and bottom 5%. The precedent of a dot held at the edge exists at rest for older history. But here it hides the peak of the stretch the viewer zoomed into, and the trim brings chips nothing: finding 8 was about rate swings just past RATE_FROM.
verifierFix: In a zoom, make must the window's points from cut = lerp(X0, X1, 0.75 * zoomWidth / fullWidth). That equals the rest fit's right quarter at full width and the whole stretch in a narrow zoom. Fit on those points without the pooled trim, and drop `zoom ||` from path() (line 637), so only pre-fitAt points are held at the edge as before.

title: trends-zoom's zoomed check 'every line point inside the plot band' can no longer fail, because path() now clamps every zoomed point; nothing guards review 3 #9
scenario: 10e130d makes path() (CumulativeChart.tsx:637) hold every point of a zoom inside [Y0, Y1]. So every `d` in `g[clip-path] path[fill="none"]` lies in [padTop, padTop+plotH] whatever the fit is, and band.out is always 0. The readout dots were already clamped. Test: revert CumulativeChart.tsx:594 to `const all = recent;`. A zoom then fits only its right quarter, which is the review 3 #9 bug. In trends-zoom's zoom into hands 24–44, the lines over about 24–39 are flattened along the edges, yet trends-zoom still passes. trends-pinch-keeps-pack also passes, at about 100%. Before this range, those points were drawn unclamped and the check failed. This is the same kind of hole as review 4 #12, and it effectively weakens a UI check, against the owner's rule.
fix: In the zoomed step, also fail when a point past its model's fitAt lies on the edge (|y − top| < 0.5 or |y − bot| < 0.5), or when the path's y differs from the value it should plot. Or remove the zoom clamp, as in the item above, so the existing in-band test fails again on a bad fit.
verifier: Confirmed. In a zoom, path() (CumulativeChart.tsx:637) clamps each value to [min(Y0,Y1), max(Y0,Y1)], so every y lies in [padTop, padTop+plotH]. The check's band at checks.mjs:3050-3061 is exactly that: clip rect y+2 to y+height-4. Every `g[clip-path] path[fill="none"]` is a model line or an EV line drawn through path(). The band path has a colour fill, and the overtake ring is a circle that is off at rest. So band.out is 0 whatever the fit. The zoomed dots were already clamped, so the dot test is vacuous too. Mutation: with `const all = recent` (a right-quarter-only zoom fit, the review 3 #9 bug), trends-zoom still passes. fix-review3 saw that bug fail this test (265 of 1,449 points out). trends-pinch-keeps-pack measures only the recent quarter's height and would read about 100%. No other check zooms. This is the same kind of hole as review 4 #12, created by the range's product change.
verifierFix: Removing the zoom clamp (item 1's fix) brings back the existing in-band test's power. If the clamp stays, make the zoomed step fail when any point past its model's fitAt sits on the band edge (|y-top|<0.5 or |y-bot|<0.5).

title: Finding 8 is only partly fixed: the first pinch step still flattens the recent quarter by about a quarter, and flat runs appear along the edges at once
scenario: This run's own trends-pinch-keeps-pack result (fix-review4/full-run.txt): 1440x900, at rest, bb/100, about 1,260 hands. One ctrl+wheel notch (deltaY −3) narrows the window from 0–1,262 to 19–1,243. The recent quarter shrinks from 340 to 250 of 396 design px (74%), so the camera eases the lines a quarter flatter on a zoom-in. The trimmed pool still holds hands 20 to about 200. That is about 15% of each line's samples, and their rates swing far wider than the recent quarter. The 5–95% trim therefore keeps them. A shorter 'All' history gives these hands a bigger share and a bigger squash, toward the base build's 52%. A lineup of late joiners does the same. In the same frame, path() starts to clamp. At rest, old stretches past fitAt that ran off the plot were clipped. They now appear at once as flat runs along the top and bottom edges, then peel off as the camera eases. trends-pinch-keeps-pack passes at ≥60%, so a step that loses 40% of the pack's height also passes.
fix: Make the zoom fit continuous with the rest fit: use the moving must cut from the first item, with no pooled trim and no zoom clamp. Then a 3% step moves the fit by about 3%. Raise trends-pinch-keeps-pack's bar to about 0.9, and also check that no edge runs appear on the first step.
verifier: Confirmed from the code and from the run's own output. fix-review4/full-run.txt line 114 shows hands 0-1262 going to 19-1243 with the recent quarter at 340 to 250 of 396 px, which is 74%. The rest fit uses the right quarter only (all = recent). One 3% notch switches line 599 to a trimmed fit of the whole window. The 5% trim drops only the most extreme samples, and hands 20-200 are about 15% of each line's samples, so their wide rates still set the range. That gives a 3% x-change a 26% y-change. It is the same symptom review 4 #8 confirmed, at half the size. A history where early hands are a larger share should do worse, but that part is reasoning, not a measurement. The edge runs are real. In the same render as the first notch, path()'s `zoom ||` clamp applies with the camera still at the rest range. Past-fitAt stretches that were clipped at rest become flat runs along both edges, and then partly peel off as the camera eases. trends-pinch-keeps-pack's 60% bar is only 8 points above the base's 52%. Same root cause as item 1.
verifierFix: Use item 1's continuous must cut, with no pooled trim and no zoom clamp. A 3% step then moves the fit by about 3%. Raise trends-pinch-keeps-pack's bar to about 0.9, and also fail it when the first step creates edge-held runs past fitAt.

title: The failed model page's line never clears, and it stays fixed over the phone's top seat (and the desktop title)
scenario:
A 390x844 phone opens a shared /#model=… link on a flaky connection. Both drawer imports fail. closeModel() clears the hash, and drawerFailed stays true. The

is fixed, z-50 and opaque. Its top is calc(var(--top-h) + 8px) = 52px. It is 32px tall, about 280px wide and centred. The oval starts about 54px down (48px padding plus 6px slack). With nine seated, the top seat's logo spans 70–118px and its clock ring 67–121px. Its action bubble spans 74–94px, from x = 225 (bubbleAt's top-seat rule). On every hand, the note hides the top 14px of the logo, the top of the ring and the top half of the bubble. Only a reload or a later successful model open clears it. When the connection comes back and a swipe loads the stats, StatsSections.tsx:57 loads the drawer chunk too. The line still says 'Model page did not load. Reload the page.' At 1440x900, --top-h is unset, so the note sits at 8px over the 'No-LLMit' title, then over the middle of the sticky bar.
fix: Clear drawerFailed after a few seconds or on a tap. Also clear it when the drawer chunk loads later: export loadDrawer and send StatsSections' preload through it. Or show the line where it covers no seat, for example just above the tab bar or in the connection bar's slot.
verifier:
Confirmed at 9e41df2. page.tsx:238 sets drawerFailed on failure, and only a later successful model open clears it. Nothing clears it on a timer or a tap. StatsSections.tsx:57's module-level import('@/components/ModelDrawer') bypasses loadDrawer, so the line stays after the chunk does load. Placement (page.tsx:578-580): fixed, z-50, bg-white, top calc(var(--top-h, 0px) + 8px). That is 52px on a 390x844 phone, where --top-h is 44px (globals.css:338), and it is 32px tall (py-1.5 plus leading-5). The oval's top is the section's 48px padding plus phone-slack/2, and phone-slack is 12px there, so the oval starts at 54px. The top seat sits at onRim(0), y 40, so its logo spans 70-118. RING_R is 27 (Player.tsx:19), so the ring spans 67-121. bubbleAt's top-seat rule puts the bubble at x+30, top-20 with leading-5, so it spans 74-94 from x 225. The

(about 52-84, x about 55-335) hides the logo's top 14px, the ring's top and the top half of every action bubble until a reload. On desktop --top-h is unset, so the line sits at 8px over the No-LLMit title. chunk-fail-says-so checks only that the line shows.
verifierFix: Move loadDrawer into a small lib module and route StatsSections' preload through it, then clear drawerFailed once the chunk resolves by any route. Also clear the line after a few seconds or on a tap. Or place it where it covers no seat, such as the connection bar's slot above the tab bar.

title: clock-stops-at-move never checks the held figure against the time left at the move
scenario: The hold is judged only on records that first appear after move+550 ms (`during`). read() records a value only when it changes. The move's commit draws the held figure at about move+250 to move+450 ms, just after the 250 ms task, so that figure is never compared with `held`. The PASS line prints the computed `held`, not what the page showed. Example (a): ReasoningPanel shows the clock only while thinking (`showShotClock = isThinking && clock !== null`). The clock then goes invisible at the move's commit, which records null before move+550. All three turns still pass, although the rule says the clock holds while the move shows. No other check reads [data-clock] in the reasoning phase: table-shot-clock and clock-after-load read only thinking, and reconnect-unseen checks only that it never goes up. Example (b): useSecondsDraw skips a stopped clock (`if (!running) return`). In the race the check sets up, the edge timer draws 42s at about move+250, before the commit. The commit draws nothing, so 42s stays for the whole hold while `held` is 43. The check passes and prints 'held 43'. stream.test.mjs:126 covers stoppedAt in stream.ts only, not the figure drawn on the page.
fix: Also judge the value in force at move+550 (the last record at or before it): require it to be non-null and equal to `held`. Keep the existing rule that nothing changes until t1. Print the observed hold value next to `held`.
verifier: Confirmed at 9e41df2. In checks.mjs, read() (6702-6704) records a value only when it changes, and `during` (6733) keeps only records first made in (move+550, t1). The move's commit draws the hold at about move+250 to move+450: useSecondsDraw's step draws on every commit and sets no timer for a stopped clock. The check's own comment allows 550 ms for that commit. So a held value drawn before move+550 is never compared with `held`, and the PASS line prints the computed `held`, not the screen. Example (a) is a mutation, not current code (ReasoningPanel.tsx:44 is `(isThinking || isReasoning)`), and it depends on timing: a late commit in turn 1 could catch it. A robust case: suppose ReasoningPanel's ms function ignored stoppedAt, as the base build held 'the last tick's' figure. The commit at about move+260 then draws 42 while `held` is 43, nothing changes until t1, and every turn passes. Example (b) passes the same way when the edge timer runs first. stream.test.mjs:126 tests clockMs in stream.ts only. table-shot-clock reads the thinking phase only, and reconnect-unseen only flags a rise between two non-null values. So nothing judges the figure on screen during the hold.
verifierFix: In the in-page promise, read [data-clock] just before feeding the next turn (at t1, about 3 s after the commit). Return that value, and require it to be visible and equal to `held`. Keep the rule that nothing changes in (move+550, t1), and print the observed hold next to `held`. Reading at t1, not at move+550, avoids a false failure when a 4x CPU commits after move+550 while the timer's 42 still shows.

title: trends-zoom's zoomed line-point rule can no longer fail, because a zoom now clamps every point into the band
scenario: 10e130d made path() hold every zoomed point in [Y0, Y1] (CumulativeChart.tsx:637). That range maps exactly to [padTop, padTop+plotH], which is the band this check reads (clip y+2 to y+h-2). So while zoomed, `band.out` is 0 by construction, and the rule that guarded review 3 #9 (the axis fits the stretch zoomed into) no longer tests anything. Regression: set CumulativeChart.tsx:594 to `const all = recent`, so a zoom is fitted like the rest view (right quarter and tips). Zoomed into hands 20–40, the axis fits hands 35–40, and most of hands 20–35 are drawn flat along the top and bottom edges. trends-zoom still passes: every point is 'inside' and the dots are clamped. trends-pinch-keeps-pack also passes, because the right quarter fits even better. At e0806b1 the same regression failed trends-zoom, because a zoom had no clamp.
fix: In the zoomed band read, also count the points held at the edge (within 0.5px of top or bot). Fail when that count exceeds what the 5–95% trim allows (about 10% of the window's points, plus points before fitAt). Or require the zoomed axis to span the window's 5th–95th percentile values.
verifier: Confirmed. Since 10e130d, path() at CumulativeChart.tsx:637 clamps every point to [min(Y0,Y1), max(Y0,Y1)] while `zoom` is set (line 501: interactive, at rest, zoomed). y() maps that range to [padTop, padTop+plotH]. trends-zoom's band is the clip rect's y+2 to y+height-2. The rect is y=padTop-2, height=plotH+4 (line 1052), so the band is exactly [padTop, padTop+plotH]. Every path the check reads (`g[clip-path] path[fill="none"]`: the EV and model lines, lines 1075-1088) goes through path(). So band.out is 0 by construction while zoomed, and the 0.5 px tolerance is far above float error. Now set line 594 to `const all = recent`. The zoom into hands 20-40 then fits only hands 35-40 plus the tips (cut = lerp(X0, X1, 0.75)), and hands 20-35 are drawn flat on the edges. trends-zoom still passes (lines and dots are clamped). trends-pinch-keeps-pack also passes, at a ratio of about 100%. trends-zoom-touch checks only the width and the page scale. At e0806b1, path() clamped only points before fitAt, so the same regression drew points outside the band and failed.
verifierFix: In the zoomed band read, also count line points within 0.5 px of top or bot. robustRange adds 8% air, so only a clamped point sits on the edge. Fail when that count exceeds what the 5-95% trim allows (about 10% of the fitted points in the window) plus the points before fitAt, and print the count.

title: The one-line-check walk test runs its own copy of the walk, so changedChecks can regress with every test green
scenario: 'no line resolves to a one-line check above it' runs the test's own walk(). That walk already excludes one-liners, using the same ONE_LINE regex that builds `ones`, so the test cannot fail for any content of checks.mjs. The only link to changedChecks is a substring match on one line (lines 69–71). It does not cover CHECK, END, ONE_LINE (checks.mjs:30) or the while line. Example: edit checks.mjs:30 to `ONE_LINE = /\}\)\);\s*$/`. table-shuffle-notice-reduced (line 2460) ends in `)));`, so changedChecks again files the Trends main step (line 2463) under it, which is review 4 #10. All three walk tests still pass.
fix: Build walk() from checks.mjs itself, as the test already does for COVERS. Extract the CHECK/END/ONE_LINE definitions and the two walk lines from the source (for example with new Function), so a change to them changes what the test runs.
verifier: Confirmed. walk() (checkCovers.test.mjs:64-68, added in 15fa567) is a copy with its own CHECK, END and ONE_LINE. `ones` (line 75) uses the same /\)\);\s*$/, so walk() can never return a one-liner's id for another line. Only a duplicate check id could fail the test, whatever checks.mjs holds. The only link to changedChecks is a substring match on checks.mjs:99 (test line 70). I ran the walk on a copy of the 9e41df2 file with ONE_LINE changed at checks.mjs:30 to /\}\)\);\s*$/. changedChecks then files line 2463 (the Trends main step) under table-shuffle-notice-reduced, because line 2460 ends in `(true)));` with no `}`. Eight lines resolve wrongly, including 648-651 to phone-table-ownership-tucked. The test's copy is unchanged, and line 99's text is unchanged, so all three walk tests stay green.
verifierFix: Build walk() from checks.mjs's own text, as the test already does for COVERS. Slice the CHECK/END/ONE_LINE declaration (line 30) and the two walk lines (97 and 99) out of src and evaluate them with new Function. Then any edit to them changes what the test runs. Drop the substring guard.

title: No check would fail if finding 4 (a stray countdown chain after the deal time changes) came back
scenario: The report names clock-after-load as the reader of 'Next hand in Ns'. clock-after-load feeds one game_state with nextHandInMs 9000 and never changes the deal time, so it cannot trigger finding 4. It is also red on both builds, so it cannot signal a regression. shuffleUnderNotice (lines 2339–2344, table-shuffle-notice) feeds exactly finding 4's trigger: end(7200), then 1 s later an outage notice and nextHandInMs 180000. But it reads only sounds and the deck. Example: restore e0806b1's countdown (React state stepped through flushSync, with the next timer set after the flush). After an outage reset, 'Next hand in Ns' alternates between about 4s and about 177s for about 4 s. Every check still passes.
fix: In shuffleUnderNotice, or in a small new countdown check, read 'Next hand in Ns' on each frame for 4 s after the reset. Require every value to match the new deal time, and never return to the old one.
verifier: Confirmed as a guard gap. The code fix itself is sound: the step draws to the DOM, there is no flushSync, and a live flag plus cleanup stop the timer. clock-after-load's countdown (checks.mjs:6640) feeds one game_state with nextHandInMs 9000 and never changes the deal time while it counts, so no old chain can exist. The run's report also has it red on both builds. The only other readers of 'Next hand in' are table-notice-says-why (1422: presence only, after the countdown ended) and reconnect-unseen (6349 strips it). shuffleUnderNotice (2339-2344) changes the deal time to 180,000 ms but reads only sounds and deck frames. So a revert of the countdown to e0806b1's flushSync stepping passes every check, though the report lists clock-after-load in #4's guard column. One correction: shuffleUnderNotice does not set up the race. Its feed lands about 1,010 ms after end() and commits well before the countdown's edge at about 1,201 ms, with no long task. So reading the text there alone would not reproduce the stray chain.
verifierFix: Add a small countdown check modelled on clock-stops-at-move. Between hands, with the deal about 7 s away, feed a game_state with a new nextHandInMs about 40 ms before a whole-second edge of the countdown. Then busy-wait about 250 ms over that edge. Record 'Next hand in Ns' on each change (MutationObserver) for 4 s. Require every value after the commit to be the new deal time's whole seconds (300 ms slack), and never the old deal time's again. Confirm that it fails on e0806b1.
